$comment: MBR-5301 membrane bioreactor train twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor from the module fact sheet and the process design; the PLC sends only what it measures and records.

identification.description: Membrane train 1 of a municipal wastewater works: submerged hollow-fibre ultrafiltration after activated sludge
identification.module: ZeeWeed 500D MBR module: PVDF hollow fibres, nominal pore 0.04 µm, outside-in, 40.0 m² per module
identification.cassette: 4 cassettes of 48 modules in one membrane tank (assumption)
identification.permeate: Reversible permeate pump on a VFD: production under suction, short backpulse in reverse
identification.air: Membrane air scour blower and aerators under each cassette
identification.plc: Train PLC: production / backpulse cycle, maintenance and recovery clean sequences, permeability records

module.source: Veolia ZeeWeed 500D Module fact sheet FSpw500D-MOD_EN (MBR column): surface area, material, pore size, fibre diameter, flow path, TMP range, max operating temperature, operating and cleaning pH, max Cl2 concentration, tensile strength (> 600 N) and module dimensions.

train.source: Train layout: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train. The ZeeWeed 500D cassette fact sheet (FSpw500D-CASS_EN) lists cassettes of up to 68 modules (68M) and 20 modules (20M).

operation.source: Design gross flux at 20 °C and nominal mixed liquor temperature: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train. Backpulse share of the operating time inside the 1-5 % range of US EPA 832-F-07-015.

permeability.source: Permeability of new (clean) fibres at 20 °C, recovery-clean trigger, very-low limit, value after the last recovery clean and normal fouling rate between maintenance cleans: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train.

viscosity.source: Water viscosity mu = A exp(B / (T - C)) (Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann fit quoted in Wikipedia 'Viscosity'). Correction to 20 °C: K20 = K(T) x mu(T) / mu(20 °C).

aeration.source: Specific air demand per m² of membrane (SADm), scour air flow and blower power: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train.

cleaning.source: Weekly maintenance clean with sodium hypochlorite, recovery clean about every 6 months or on the permeability trigger, hypochlorite then citric acid: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train. Hypochlorite and citric acid are the usual chemicals (US EPA 832-F-07-015); the recovery clean hypochlorite stays at the 1,000 ppm Cl2 maximum of the module fact sheet.

process.source: Mixed liquor suspended solids, time-to-filter of the mixed liquor and permeate turbidity of a healthy train: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train. (US EPA 832-F-07-015 reports one large ZeeWeed plant averaging 6,400 mg/L MLSS.)

demo.note: Demo only: the plant clock runs 5040 times faster, so one week between maintenance cleans passes in two minutes of real time and the permeability sawtooth is visible.

points.label: Transmembrane pressure (suction, as a positive number)
Mixed liquor suspended solids in the membrane tank
Time-to-filter of the mixed liquor (last lab test)
Flux at which the last MC permeability check ran
Temperature during the last MC check
TMP just before the last maintenance clean
TMP just after the last maintenance clean
Hours since the last maintenance clean
Permeability at 20 °C measured after the last recovery clean
Hours since the last recovery clean

twin_model.source: Alert limits: assumption: typical value, replace with the supplier's process design / O&M manual for your train. TMP limit of the module: Veolia ZeeWeed 500D Module fact sheet FSpw500D-MOD_EN (MBR column) (55 kPa). Permeate turbidity below 0.5 NTU is Veolia's typical ZeeWeed MBR effluent claim; 0.2 NTU is an early-warning assumption.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

irreversible_fouling.name: Irreversible fouling (scale, organics the cleans no longer remove)
irreversible_fouling.symptoms: permeability after cleans lower each time, maintenance clean recovers little

poor_filterability.name: Poor sludge filterability (bulking, foaming, high SMP)
poor_filterability.symptoms: permeability falls fast between cleans, time-to-filter up

air_scour_low.name: Air scour reduced (blocked aerators, blower or valve fault)
air_scour_low.symptoms: SADm low, permeability falls fast between cleans

sludging.name: Module sludging (solids packed between the fibres)
sludging.symptoms: MLSS high, TMP jumps, permeability very low

peak_flux.name: Flux above design (storm flow with a cassette out)
peak_flux.symptoms: flux per m² in service above the design flux, TMP up, permeability normal

mc_skipped.name: Maintenance cleans skipped (sequence or dosing failure)
mc_skipped.symptoms: hours since the last MC grow, permeability drifts down
